name: Alchemist's Laboratory
reason: A facility inside the Elysian Keep (source Immortal Mansion) was rendered with the plain descriptive English name 'Alchemist's Laboratory' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A sealed facility within the Elysian Keep, coveted alongside the Armory by the Soul Realm masters who raided the keep. Even as the keep's temporary master, Zane could not access it, though a single elixir from it could have made his strength skyrocket.

name: Pikes
reason: Generic plural weapon noun, not a named entity.

name: Five-Clawed Golden Dragon
reason: The source weapon name 'Five-clawed Golden Dragon' (Xu Xiu's weapon, chs 115-189, aligned with Eps 154-201) was carried over literally.
description: A powerful dragon-shaped weapon wielded in the source by the enemy commander Xu Xiu; individually far stronger than the massed lesser weapons deployed against Zane in the same battle.

name: Cerulean Ward
reason: A defensive barrier in the Elysian Keep arc was given the invented Western-fantasy name 'Cerulean Ward'; no specific source term was identified in the evidence.
description: Seymour's blue defensive barrier at the Elysian Keep; the black hawk's impact fractured its surface with spiderwebs of red cracks (Ep 156).

name: Former Host
reason: Generic referential title for the Elysian Keep's previous owner, not a stable entity name.

name: Cloud and Flying Birds Picture
reason: The source contemplation picture 'Flying Birds in Clouds Diagram' was localized as 'Cloud and Flying Birds Picture'; the source candidate's chapter range (147-953) aligns exactly with the episode range (162-976).
description: A high-ranked contemplation picture from the Elysian Keep, in the source second only to the Sun, Moon, and Stars Diagram; used for comprehension training and referenced again in the late episodes.

name: Flesh-Honing Stage
reason: The source body-cultivation term 'Flesh Refining Stage' was localized as 'Flesh-Honing Stage' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: An early body-tempering cultivation stage below the Adept levels, referenced when recalling a cultivator's progression (Ep 164).

name: Nine-Day Cycle Picture
reason: The source contemplation picture 'Nine-Heavens Samsara Diagram' (ch 147, aligned with Ep 164) was localized as 'Nine-Day Cycle Picture'.
description: The third-ranked contemplation picture of the Elysian Keep, with intricate, densely packed levels. The Warrior devoted half a year to contemplating it (Ep 164), and it resurfaces when a terrified woman secures it in Ep 976.

name: Zane's Corrupt Vitality
reason: Possessive descriptive phrase, not a standalone entity; the underlying energy is covered by the canonical 'Vitality'.

name: Steven
reason: The source traitor He Yuetian (ch 160: defected from the Blue Cloud Sect and slaughtered its disciples across the Eastern Domain) was fully localized to the US-style name 'Steven Hill'.
description: A dark chapter in Skyreach Sect history: a prodigy who reached the Soul Realm nine years after joining, then betrayed the Sect and slaughtered its disciples across the Eastern Territory. Killing him cost the Sect three Saints, after which it adopted the rule that a disciple's character matters more than talent.

name: Zane’s Vitality
reason: Possessive phrase, not a standalone entity; the energy itself is covered by the canonical 'Vitality'.

name: Sunspire Peak
reason: One of the Skyreach Sect's ranked peaks (from the source's 33 peaks of the Blue Cloud Sect) given the invented Western name 'Sunspire Peak'; its specific source peak was not identified.
description: The fourth-ranked peak of the sect and House Brandt territory. It was among the top-ten peaks that Misty Peak drew as first-round opponents in the All Peaks Competition (Ep 235).

name: Deathly Palm
reason: A source martial technique was localized under the invented name 'Deathly Palm'; no specific source term was identified in the evidence.
description: A palm technique whose user boasts that no Adept has ever withstood it (Ep 189).

name: Violet Blades
reason: Nolan's projectile weapons were localized with the name 'Violet Blades', confirmed as the correct canonical name by the master sheet.
description: A swarm of humming energy blades wielded by Nolan as projectile weapons, materialized in the air and shot at Jace in Ep 19.

name: House Zane
issues: Extraction artifact: the string comes from sentence boundaries such as 'As the former heir of the House, Zane knew...' (Ep 19). No 'House Zane' exists; Zane's family is House Lowell (source Luo Family).
reason: Not an entity; a false positive from 'the House, Zane' crossing a comma boundary.

name: Cerulean Blade
issues: Name reused for two apparently different swords: Zane's father's blade (Ep 19, threatened against Evil Jace) and Finn Donovan's blade carried on his back (Ep 240) — possible merged entity.
reason: A sword name invented for the Western fantasy register; no source term was identified in the evidence.
description: A named sword appearing twice with different owners: Zane's father swore to cut down Evil Jace with his Cerulean Blade (Ep 19), and Finn Donovan of Skytop Peak later appears with the Cerulean Blade strapped to his back (Ep 240).

name: Lord Moon
reason: Honorific form of James Moon, head of House Moon (source Mo Family). Episode scenes (James nearly killing Zane, stopped by the hatchet-wielding Tyson) match source Mo Xiuyan, the Mo family father whom Shi Hu and Cang Qiu face down (chs 192-194). The mixed episode pronoun signal (m2/f2) is noise from surrounding dialogue.
description: Title by which guests address James Moon, Yates's father and host of the House Moon gathering.

name: Yates’
reason: Possessive surface form of Yates, the young spear-wielding noble of House Moon; matches source Mo Yu, the young Mo family disciple of the aligned chapters (182-194).

name: Mount Frostfire
reason: A mountain location given an invented Western-fantasy name; no specific source counterpart was identified in the evidence.
description: A mountain location mentioned once in Ep 198.

name: First-Level Adept
reason: Compositional rank phrase of the Adept Realm (source Xiantian levels), not a standalone entity; covered by the base realm term.

name: Seventh-Level Adept
issues: Rank phrasing drifts between 'Seventh-Level Adept' (Ep 199) and 'Level Seven Adept' (Eps 235, 429) for the same rank — style inconsistency, not separate entities.
reason: Compositional rank phrase of the Adept Realm, not a standalone entity; covered by the base realm term.

name: Signal Talisman
reason: A talisman-based signalling device from the source setting kept under the literal descriptive name 'Signal Talisman'.
description: A communication talisman used to call for help; Ingrid activated hers to summon aid when threatened (Eps 201-202).

name: Moon Mansion
issues: The Ep 338 context line refers to the 'Crimson Moon Mansion' (the Seventh Prince's party venue), a different location caught by substring overlap; do not merge the two.
reason: The residence of House Moon (source Mo Family compound) was localized as 'Moon Mansion' to match the house's localized name.
description: The residence of House Moon, where Zane was directed to the guest hall under his mysterious savior's protection, and where a steward tallied the 336 houses of the compound that Zane had destroyed (Eps 205-207).

name: Woodcutter's Axe
reason: Likely adapts the source's 'Woodcutter of West Mountain' (ch 192, aligned with Ep 206); the adaptation uses the plain descriptive name for Tyson's weapon.
description: The unassuming yet lethal axe carried by the burly Tyson (source Shi Hu), its blade flickering with red light; he presses it against James Moon's sword to stop him from killing Zane (Eps 206-207).

name: Uncle George
reason: Honorific form of George, Ingrid's protector; matches source Cang Qiu, whom Zhu Qianning (Ingrid) addresses identically as 'Uncle Cang Qiu' in the parallel scene (ch 193 vs Ep 207).

name: Golden Cicadas
reason: The source demon beast 'Golden Cicada' (ch 198, whose wings forge the Jade Wave sword) was carried over literally; the dossier form is simply the plural.
description: A rare level-seven demon beast whose tough, innately sharp wings can cut iron like mud and are prized for forging blades (Ep 210).

name: Beacon Spear
reason: A named spear from the competition arc given an invented Western name; no specific source term was identified in the evidence.
description: A spear wielded by one of Zane's opponents, left shattered on the ground by Zane's sword (Ep 220).

name: Zane's Student ID
reason: The sect identity token that records a disciple's points and balance was re-imagined as a 'Student ID' for the adaptation's school-flavored register.
description: Zane's sect identification, which flashes to record transactions such as his massive balance of Crystal Cubes (Eps 44, 221).

name: Steward Rogers
issues: Distinct from the off-screen 'Roger' (Zane's friend, Ep 399) noted in the master sheet — similar names, different characters; do not merge.
reason: A minor sect steward given the US-style surname 'Rogers'; no specific source counterpart was identified in the evidence.
description: A steward who grew used to Zane's rapid cultivation progress but remained troubled by it; he reported his concerns, to no effect (Ep 231).

name: Cloud Road Zane
issues: Concatenation artifact of 'Cloud Road' + 'Zane'; the real entity is the Cloud Road trial dimension (source 'Green Cloud Road'), covered by its own entry.
reason: Extraction artifact, not an entity.

name: Silas
reason: The sneering mentor of Sea Peak (source 'Mentor Wang' of Hou Haifeng / Thick Sea Peak, a 'lean little old man' matching the episodes' 'skinny old man') was localized to 'Silas', a sharp-sounding name fitting his mocking demeanor.
description: Master of Sea Peak, a skinny old man who ridicules Misty Peak's seven-man roster before the All Peaks Competition and backs his favored inner disciple York to crush Zane in the arena (Eps 234-241).

name: Level Seven Adept
issues: Same rank is also phrased 'Seventh-Level Adept' (Ep 199) — style inconsistency, not separate entities.
reason: Compositional rank phrase of the Adept Realm, not a standalone entity; covered by the base realm term.

name: Azure Peak
reason: One of the Skyreach Sect's ranked peaks (from the source's 33 peaks) given the invented Western name 'Azure Peak'; its specific source peak was not identified.
description: A top-ten peak of the sect and Langdon's home peak; its privileged disciples faced Misty Peak in the first round of the All Peaks Competition (Eps 235-238).

name: Deadly Swamp Trap
reason: The source binding technique 'Swamp Trap' (Zhou Tong's move, ch 223, aligned with Ep 236) was localized with the intensifier 'Deadly'.
description: A binding technique in which the user's Vitality oozes across the ground and wraps an opponent's legs in thick, heavy layers, cementing them in place. Reputedly no Adept can escape it; it was used against Zane in the All Peaks Competition (Eps 236-237).

name: Lady Hawkins
issues: Episode pronoun signal (m3/f0) is noise from nearby male characters; she is explicitly an old woman ('her', 'old woman with a cane') in both episodes and source (Granny Hua), so gender is Female. Also, Ep 239 retains the un-localized source honorific 'Mistress Hua' alongside 'Lady Hawkins' — a localization leak.
reason: Source 'Granny Hua', the aged mentor of Nine Zhang Peak, was localized as 'Lady Hawkins', with her peak rendered as Ninety-Foot Peak (nine zhang is roughly ninety feet).
description: The elderly, cane-carrying master of Ninety-Foot Peak, whom even the most powerful saints address with deference. Though her own cultivation is modest, her seniority makes her untouchable; she gloats over Mack's crystal-boosted win against Misty Peak's Eliot and calls their disciples trash (Eps 239-240).

name: Vitality-infused
reason: Adjectival fragment, not an entity; the underlying energy is the canonical 'Vitality'.

name: Mid-Grade Spirit Weapon
reason: Grade-qualified variant of the canonical tier-2 term 'Spirit Weapon', not a separate entity.
